title: One Sentence Each · Classic
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play One Sentence Each · Classic with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Choose two players and a simple starting situation. The lead and partner alternate one sentence each until they have said four sentences. The four sentences form one coherent story with an ending. Each player takes two turns. Give the lead one point for each successful turn. Highest score wins; ties are shared.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 2–8 players; materials: None.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In One Sentence Each, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
The group ends the round before anyone plays.
The four sentences form one coherent story with an ending.
recall.why: The four sentences form one coherent story with an ending.
